response: Yes, there is oxidative stress in uremia. The increased levels of autoxidation products of both carbohydrates and lipids in uremic plasma suggest a broad derangement in non-enzymatic biochemistry, which implicates oxidative stress. This is further supported by the increased levels of advanced glycosylation end-products (AGEs) in blood and tissues, which are a result of oxidative stress and non-enzymatic reactions involving carbohydrates and lipids. Therefore, oxidative stress is indeed present in uremia, and it may play a role in the pathogenesis and progression of the disease.
